title: Tesla's Optimus robot with Grok shown on video. We're not impressed.
key_facts: A video shared on X by Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff shows a next-generation Tesla Optimus humanoid in gold covering with more human-like hands, now running xAI's Grok voice mode so it can answer spoken questions.
In the clip the robot responds slowly and needs several prompts before taking a few steps toward a kitchen to fetch a Coke; the video ends before it does.
Mashable judges it a modest step beyond earlier human-assisted demos and far from Musk's goal of selling millions a year.
Benioff called it a 'productivity game-changer' tackling human work for 200,000 to 500,000 dollars; Mashable notes he recently cut 4,000 Salesforce support jobs in favour of AI agents.
Optimus is still a prototype; the article says production is scheduled to start in 2026 and references Tesla's Master Plan Part 4.
The article's references (Master Plan Part 4, the Salesforce job cuts, 'We, Robot' event 'last year') match September 2025, not October 2026.
quote_evidence: The video, shared by Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff, shows the next-gen Optimus in new, gold attire, with several new visual details including more human-like hands. More importantly, Optimus now features Grok's voice mode
Optimus appears slow to respond, requiring several vocal nudges to start performing a fairly simple task — going to the kitchen and fetching a Coke.
why_it_matters_hint: A public look at Optimus talking via Grok shows how far it still is from useful autonomy.
event_date: unclear; article content points to September 2025
notes: Likely an older Mashable article re-dated in the feed: it cites Master Plan Part 4 and the Salesforce 4,000 job cuts (both Sep 2025) and says production is 'scheduled to start in 2026'. Nothing in the text is dated October 2026. Flag for the QA record as a possible re-date.
